shots.title: Problem and boundary
shots.screen: Synthetic Jira work item / PermitGuard title and site-procedure notice
shots.narration: In group lockout work, a permit record must not hide the people whose personal locks still protect them. PermitGuard brings that coordination into Jira. The site procedure remains authoritative.

shots.title: Identify the deployed build
shots.screen: PGSAMPLE-2 ACTIVE panel; footer 5.16.0 / UI 5f92b0c1b926; own-lock rail and top release strip
shots.narration: Here is the deployed development build and our synthetic active permit. Work-start readiness and release readiness are separate. The release blocker stays visible at the top. Historical preview is labelled; actions wait for current authorization.
shots.evidence: 5.16 footer/panel observed by owner 24 Nov; prior broad core acceptance was 5.15 on 22 Nov

shots.title: Native Rovo, release first
shots.screen: One PermitGuard Judge; new chat: Is PGSAMPLE-2 cleared?; actual tool response
shots.narration: Ask the native Judge whether this work item is cleared. It leads with release not cleared, then gives the narrower work-start result. It reads the same deterministic service as the panel, rather than granting safety authority.
shots.evidence: Native action path accepted; not MCP transport proof

shots.title: Personal-lock barrier — read-only walkthrough
shots.screen: Inspect current personal-lock records and top release result; source-labelled shared-lock guard inset if needed. No seeding, phase change, lock removal or close attempt.
shots.narration: Personal-lock records remain attributable. A worker removing their own lock does not clear someone else’s remaining record. The shared service enforces that barrier. Here we inspect the current record and the rule without changing locks or pretending a simulated crew is another real person.
shots.evidence: Current UI read plus labelled source rule; no new live release sequence claimed

shots.title: Authorized reread in another tab
shots.screen: Two read-only views of the same issue, explicitly labelled manual Refresh; show automatic invalidation only if genuinely recorded
shots.narration: The other tab rereads authorized state. Here we show manual Refresh explicitly. Realtime carries invalidation hints, not permit records or safety authority; we do not claim delivery that this recording has not shown.
shots.evidence: Read-only reread; no fabricated change/automatic delivery

shots.title: Human-only activation boundary
shots.screen: Source/README action diagram: GET readiness, CREATE PENDING, no agent confirmation tool
shots.narration: The agent has no confirmation tool. Its activation action can only propose pending work for a named human. Equipment confirmation remains human-only; a QR or photo does not independently prove presence.
shots.evidence: Implemented/local-tested rule; not a new live activation demonstration

shots.title: Real Forge MCP read — owner receipt
shots.screen: 5 seconds GET-only rovo:mcp declaration, 20 seconds legible redacted owner receipt (actual check_readiness_development name, input, scoped result), 5 seconds owner-reported OFF/grant cleanup. Label Historical owner receipt · 24 Nov 21:06:40 UTC · not live Inspector footage.
shots.narration: PermitGuard also exposes a Forge MCP server. In this owner-documented development run, Inspector discovered one read-only tool. One call returned work-start-only clearance, not release clearance, at revisions twenty-two and six. Consent still showed broad app permissions. Exposure was disabled and the client grant removed afterward.
shots.evidence: PASS_OWNER_RECEIPT: genuine owner-run discovery/read, historical text evidence only; no new call, activation, screenshot or filmed Inspector interaction claimed

shots.title: Architecture and close
shots.screen: README architecture, public MIT repository and remaining release blocker
shots.narration: Forge stores bounded records and checks revisions before writes. Jira access remains user-authorized. No external app runtime or SQL is needed. Named humans and the site procedure remain in control.
